smm_pool.title: We’re running an A/B test on human and AI involvement in hiring
smm_pool.text: We’re hiring for two roles, and trying two very different experiments We’ve spent many hours debating when, where, and how AI should fit into our hiring process. As a small team with a lot of ambition, we are trying to level up, and hiring is ripe for this level of innovation. At the same time, we want to keep a high level of human touch and judgment in hiring. It’s such a key area, when each hire has a huge impact on our goals and culture. For a long time, our process rested on the idea that a Buffer teammate would carefully read every application. That came from a good place, and we’re proud of it. At today’s volume, though, it has meant long waits for candidates and stretched-thin hiring managers. We know we need to modernize our process so we can do better, both for the people applying to Buffer and for our hiring managers. On the flip side, if you’ve looked for a job lately, you know the market is tough right now. It can be incredibly competitive, and at times fairly inhuman. And, it’s been tough to be on the hiring side in its own way. More and more of the applications we see are largely written by AI. We understand why; applying to a job (or many) can be draining, and job seekers need to preserve their time and mental health. But that has made it harder for us to spot the thoughtful and personal applications, and get back to people in a reasonable amount of time. So, we’re testing two ways to get there. We’re opening two roles, with very different application processes, as an experiment. Our goal is to learn as much as we can about the pros and cons of each approach, as we work to build a thoughtful hiring process that’s both efficient and deeply caring in a post-AI world. Here’s how we’re running these experiments. Experiment 1: Engineering Manager: a much lighter way to raise your hand. For our EM role, we’re making it much easier to say “I’m interested.” A short intro instead of a long application. Our applications have always asked a lot: a series of detailed questions about the work and the person applying. We loved getting to know people that way, but it was a big investment for the candidate, and it stings when it doesn’t work out. This time, we’re just asking for your profile and a short introduction, so we can do more of the work to understand your experience before asking more of you. smm_pool.title: We are Retiring Start Page: Why and What to Expect
smm_pool.text: As Buffer has continued to support the individuals, creators, and small and medium businesses who use us, we've had to balance being a relatively small team with making tough decisions. We've had to make one of these recently. After careful deliberation as a team, we've decided to retire Start Page. If you've built a Start Page with us, thank you. Creators, small businesses, and nonprofits have used it as a front door to their work since 2021. Many of our customers were just getting started with their online journey, and a full website can be expensive and fiddly to maintain. Start Page provided a simple, flexible page anyone could build in minutes and share across their social profiles. We don't take ending that lightly, which is why we're giving several months' notice, firm dates, and multiple options to make the transition as hassle-free as possible Here's the timeline: November 4, 2026: We've stopped allowing the creation of new Start Pages November 30, 2026: You'll have tools to move your page somewhere else. February 2, 2027: We'll begin taking down Start Pages that haven't been migrated somewhere else. I'd like to elaborate on why we're doing this, the plan moving forward, and what options we plan to have available. Why we're doing this Having one link that holds everything (also referred to as a link-in-bio tool) is still useful in today's social space. So why are we moving away from it? For us at Buffer, three things have become hard to ignore. We've focused Buffer on our core strengths outside of Start Page. Buffer is a social media toolkit: we help you plan, publish, and learn from your content, and engage with your community across the social channels you use. While Start Page lives in your bio, it sits off to the side of all that. We've wanted to work on Start Page, but it takes away from Buffer's strengths and focus. From a capabilities perspective, Start Page has fallen behind, and catching up would cost us the things you rely on. Link-in-bio and microsite tools have come a long way since 2021, and Start Page hasn't kept pace. Making it best-in-class would mean pulling several teammates away from other key, much-requested improvements to other core Buffer features. We don't think that's the right trade for most of our customers. It's challenging to run well as a small, nimble team.
